Nut trade is the circulation layer.

Production creates the crop. Capital finances the system. Trade moves the inventory into price discovery, demand, warehousing, and liquidity. This page tracks that movement.

Core framing Trade data is where a physical asset meets the market.

For any warehouse receipt, commodity NAV model, or tokenized inventory design, the relevant question is not only “what exists?” but also “where can it clear, at what price, through which corridor, and with what concentration risk?” [12]

05 · WHY THIS MATTERS

Trade turns inventory into a financeable object.

A commodity token, warehouse receipt, or inventory-backed NAV only works if the underlying stock can move through real corridors with observable demand, acceptable basis risk, and tolerable concentration. Trade is the circulation and liquidity layer of the RWA stack.

Oracle designDerived unit values and route dispersion help frame mark-to-market references.
Collateral haircutsConcentrated destination exposure or hub dependence can justify harsher risk cuts.
Warehouse locationDemand hubs and processing hubs matter more than poetic geography.
Exit liquidityThe corridor set tells you who can realistically clear inventory if forced to sell.

Method discipline

CY vs. MYCalendar-year customs flows and marketing-year USDA balances are different datasets. This page keeps route charts on CY2024 for comparability.
HS codesShelled almonds (HS 080212) are not the same product as in-shell almonds. Product definition is part of the analysis.
Gross flowsWITS labels these flows as gross exports/imports. Re-exports and redistribution can appear in the data.
Customs valueUnit values here are customs value divided by quantity. They are not farm-gate price, spot price, or a perfected NAV mark.
06 · SOURCES

Primary data & definitions

USDA FAS supplies the policy and market backdrop. WITS / UN Comtrade supplies comparable bilateral customs records and global importer/exporter rankings.
